summary: 110-foot tower moved from Southampton County, Virginia, by CRATA; restored and opened to the public in November 2025 at Overlook Park on Lake Martin.

corrections.why: The register names the origin and the site; Jimmy K. Lanier is the tower's name, not a place. The register dates the start of the move to 2021, not its completion.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lake Martin magazine calls the tower newly constructed and says volunteers reconstructed it; the register says it was moved from Virginia and fully restored. Both could fit a rebuild from moved parts. The magazine does not mention Virginia. The conflict is not settled: the Virginia origin rests on the register alone.

notes_for_editor: The Virginia origin and the 1930s date rest on the NHLR page alone. Searches found no second source. The Virginia lookout list at https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/va/va-st/ has no Vicksville or Sedley entry in its relocated section. The search summary called the Virginia origin a mix-up; that is the register's claim, not a verified fact, and the magazine's newly constructed framing is a real conflict, not a settled one. The Lake Martin magazine article 'A Towering Legacy' returned HTTP 429 twice and was not read. The climbing article is undated in our copy; its caption says the tower was to open 'this summer', so it was likely written before the November 2025 opening. Height 33.5 m is converted from the 110 ft overall height; the cab floor height is not given. Climbing is not stated; the story says only that it is open to the public. No source found explains the Lanier name. Source 3 is about the Smith Mountain tower; the story uses it for Lanier's CRATA role and his idea to restore that tower. The source 2 title matches the page title, 'Climbing New Heights'.
